question: For the equations ax + (a² + 1)y = 4 and 4x + ay = a², which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: { If } a = 6, { then } x = (325)/(28), y = (-25)/(28) { are the solutions.}
{ If } a = 6, { then } x = 48, y = 4 { are the solutions.} \\
{ If } a = -12, { then } x = 48, y = 4 { are the solutions.}

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Test the options directly by substituting the values into the given equations.

Check the values: a = −12, x = 48, and y = 4.

Equation 2: 4x + ay = 4(48) + (−12)(4) = 192 − 48 = 144. Also a² = (−12)² = 144. (Matches)

Equation 1: ax + (a² + 1)y = (−12)(48) + (144 + 1)(4) = −576 + 580 = 4. (Matches)

**∴ The correct answer is If a = −12, then x = 48, y = 4 are the solutions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation (i): ax + (a² + 1)y = 4

Equation (ii): 4x + ay = a²

**Calculations:**

⇒ From equation (ii), 4x = a² − ay ⇒ x = (a² − ay) ÷ 4

⇒ Substitute x in equation (i):

⇒ a[(a² − ay) ÷ 4] + (a² + 1)y = 4

⇒ a³ − a²y + 4y(a² + 1) = 16

⇒ a³ − a²y + 4a²y + 4y = 16

⇒ y(3a² + 4) = 16 − a³

⇒ y = (16 − a³) ÷ (3a² + 4)

⇒ Now check for a = −12:

⇒ y = [16 − (−12)³] ÷ [3(−12)² + 4]

⇒ y = (16 + 1728) ÷ (3 × 144 + 4)

⇒ y = 1744 ÷ 436 = 4

⇒ Substitute y = 4 and a = −12 in equation (ii):

⇒ 4x + (−12)(4) = (−12)²

⇒ 4x − 48 = 144

⇒ 4x = 192

⇒ x = 48

**∴ The correct answer is If a = −12, then x = 48, y = 4 are the solutions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

A system of two linear equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂ can have a unique solution, infinite solutions, or no solution depending on the coefficients.

Unique Solution Condition

The system has a unique solution if and only if a₁ ÷ a₂ ≠ b₁ ÷ b₂. In this case, the intersecting lines meet at exactly one point (x, y).

Substitution Method

To solve by substitution, express one variable in terms of the other using one equation and substitute this expression into the second equation to find the exact value.
